markdown_report:
At 20% progress, prioritize a controlled test of **recent-anchored lexical support**, retaining simpler pooling and objective-only alternatives as eligible winners.

Starting-point insights:
- Distinct-ID exclusion prevents self-matches, but maximum similarity measures strongest resemblance rather than recurrence frequency. Different IDs can also represent near-duplicate editions.
- Confidence outside normalization preserves evidence strength. However, multiplicative agreement can suppress useful signals through concentration alone.
- Electronics has 16.04% negative-over-positive training pairs and a negative tenth-percentile margin. This motivates objective controls without explaining validation errors.

Related-work insights:
- [ICSRec](https://doi.org/10.1145/3616855.3635773) motivates separating intentions across subsequences. Shared-target alignment remains an intent proxy.
- [Hierarchical long/short-term modeling](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) and [PAN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.15346) motivate matching historical preferences to multiple recent events. Neither validates lexical gates.
- [SIM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.05639) selects candidate-relevant history. Its candidate-conditioned query differs from the proposed recent-history query.
- [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) motivates calibrated BCE with more negatives. Loss and negative-count effects require separate controls.

These insights organize into evidence specificity, temporal selection, and candidate discrimination:

| Method | Evidence | Temporal selection | Objective |
|---|---|---|---|
| SASRec | Learned interactions | Causal attention | Baseline BCE |
| Starting residual | Distinct-item lexical resemblance | Recency decay | Multi-negative CE |
| Proposed residual | Resemblance linked to recent distinct IDs | Recent anchors plus decay | Same CE |

Three candidate ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Detailed positive and negative reasons appear in implementation notes.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recent-anchored lexical support | 3/6/7/5/5 | Targets broad association and stale evidence through an inspectable comparison | Incremental; extra attenuation may explain any apparent benefit |
| Generalized-BCE control | 2/7/3/8/3 | Established, inexpensive discrimination alternative | Does not explicitly address two user failures; ineligible as the selected research idea alone |
| Learned recent/history routing | 4/7/8/6/7 | Expresses multiple persistent preferences and recent changes | More parameters and ambiguity before simpler controls establish value |

**Selected algorithm.** Preserve fixed training-only TF–IDF. Within each causal twenty-event prefix, compute distinct-ID whole-window agreement u and agreement a with the last three events. Pool with weights r·u·a and apply support confidence after normalization. Because anchors are a subset of the window, a≤u: compare against r·u² before attributing gains to recent relevance.

The proposal explicitly targets broad associations lacking specific evidence and older or isolated interactions carrying forward. Shared multi-negative training targets weak sampled pair separation; neither mechanism establishes practical compatibility or unmet needs.

Compare objective-only SASRec, starting support, anchored support, and squared-support control under equal remaining-budget caps. Include recent-only and random/old-anchor frozen-model diagnostics. Select complete four-category runs solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Inspect support, effective pooling size, duplicate concentration, fused margins, and rank changes. Historical scores and literature results establish no improvement for this proposal.

idea.description: Test recent-anchored fixed lexical fusion for per-dataset SASRec against objective-only, starting repeated-support, and squared-support controls. Historical text receives recency-weighted whole-window distinct-ID agreement multiplied by agreement with distinct recent anchors; confidence remains outside pool normalization. Treat temporal relevance and extra concentration as competing explanations.
idea.motivation: The selected idea explicitly addresses two diagnosed user failures: broad historical associations outranking more specific matches, and older or isolated interactions carrying forward despite recent activity. Distinct-ID lexical resemblance supplies a limited specificity proxy, while recent-anchor agreement suppresses disconnected historical clusters. Uniform multi-negative training targets the model-facing weak sampled training-pair separation, especially Electronics, as a hypothesis. Maximum resemblance does not measure recurrence frequency, and distinct IDs do not guarantee distinct product families. Neither histories nor lexical agreement establish compatibility, ownership, quantity requirements, satisfied needs, complements, or simulator traits.
idea.implementation_notes:
Protocol: retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl as separate category models with unchanged baseline routing and splits. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution, and effective SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Save checkpoints, text artifacts, configuration, diagnostics, and generated working/predict.py beneath the trial directory. Use only permitted histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps. Generic examples do not authorize review ratings/text or item ratings/categories/prices/stores. Do not access hidden test files, fetch datasets or pretrained weights, or modify the host evaluator. No implementation, execution, successful parity check, or validation improvement is claimed.

Text features: preserve the starting implementation's deterministic training-visible TF–IDF preprocessing for attribution. If implementing anew, use lowercase Unicode alphanumeric tokens; compute document frequency over complete permitted title-plus-description documents from items occurring in training histories. Define N as that training-item count. Build at most 30,000 vocabulary entries, ordered by descending document frequency with lexical tie-breaking, excluding tokens with df/N > 0.20. Retain the first 32 surviving tokens from title followed by description, collapse repeated tokens to binary term frequency, and apply IDF = log((1+N)/(1+df))+1. L2-normalize rows with epsilon 1e-8; missing or filtered text yields exactly zero. Map items outside the fitted training-item scope to zero text rows rather than using held-out interactions to extend the vocabulary. Persist vocabulary, document frequencies, IDF, filtering, row mappings, catalog scope, tokenizer rules, and truncation order. Record any difference from an existing incumbent; a changed preprocessing pipeline requires a newly matched starting comparator.

Causal features: at each supervised position use the sequence through that position, excluding its shifted next-item target and future events. Take its last twenty nonpadding events, retaining event order and repeated IDs. Define anchors as its last three events, without extending backward when IDs repeat. For event j, r_j=exp(-age_j/5), where age zero denotes the latest event. Let u_j be maximum nonnegative TF–IDF cosine to any window event with a different item ID, and a_j maximum cosine to any anchor with a different item ID; empty eligible sets return zero. Mask all equal-ID matches, not merely diagonal positions. Missing-text events supply zero agreement but remain in the confidence denominator. Define w_j=r_j*u_j*a_j, q=normalize_or_zero(sum_j w_j*v_j), and c=sum_j w_j/max(sum_j r_j,1e-8). Repeated occurrences of one ID cannot activate support alone, but can amplify support supplied by another ID. Explicitly measure that limitation.

Dependence and controls: anchors are a subset of the window, so 0 <= a_j <= u_j <= 1. Thus u_j*a_j <= u_j²; the two agreement factors are dependent, and their product is not evidence from two independent sources. Primary conditions are A: objective-only SASRec; B: starting support w=r*u; C: anchored support w=r*u*a; D: squared support w=r*u². For B, C, and D use the same q normalization and c=sum(w)/sum(r). C versus B combines temporal selection with attenuation; C versus D is a necessary stronger concentration control, although it still does not match confidence or effective pooling size exactly. Do not tune an exponent to match validation outcomes after inspecting them. Record normalized weights p_j=w_j/sum(w), effective event pool size 1/sum(p_j²), and effective distinct-ID pool size after aggregating p by ID; report unavailable when support mass is zero. Maxima represent strongest resemblance, not a count of independent recurring interests.

Scoring: s_i=h dot e_i + alpha*c*(q dot v_i), alpha=2*A*sigmoid(b), initialized with sigmoid(b)=0.05. Calibrate category-specific A=max(1,median absolute collaborative positive-minus-uniform-negative margin) using the first 10,000 eligible training positions, or all available if fewer, from a compatible frozen baseline checkpoint in deterministic order. Record the checkpoint, ordered positions, exclusions, sampled IDs, and separate calibration generator seed 42; charge all work to the budget. Share A across residual conditions within category. If preserving a different incumbent calibration, use it for all residual conditions and document it rather than changing calibration and anchoring simultaneously. If no compatible baseline checkpoint exists, predeclare A=1 for every residual condition and label this a fixed-scale experiment, avoiding an undeclared baseline training expense. Since c is in [0,1] and cosine is in [-1,1], pairwise residual changes are bounded by 2*alpha*c for a fixed prefix. These bounds do not guarantee useful scale; report alpha, c, residual variance, residual-to-collaborative-margin scale, and actual rank changes.

Objective and sampling: use 32 distinct uniform negatives per valid target in all four primary conditions. Exclude padding, target, and IDs observed in that causal prefix only; never consult future interactions or held-out labels. Draw by uniform rejection sampling without replacement using a dedicated generator seeded 42. Use every eligible item if fewer than 32 exist, mask unused slots, and omit positions with no eligible negative. Save or deterministically regenerate candidate streams shared across conditions. Optimize cross-entropy with positive index zero and temperature 1, averaging over eligible positions. No LogQ correction is used: this is a sampled ranking surrogate, not an unbiased full-softmax estimator. Observed-positive filtering does not eliminate latent false negatives. Keep backbone, optimizer, learning rate, regularization, batch size, sequence length, loader ordering, validation schedule, and checkpoint rule unchanged; record resolved settings from the host template. Separate model and sampling RNG streams; initialize shared backbone weights identically. Do not add semi-hard mining, learned text encoders, auxiliary losses, or architecture changes in this experiment.

Objective alternatives: BCE, generalized BCE, and sampled softmax remain plausible follow-up winners; no cited paper establishes a universal choice here. The primary family holds sampled CE and negative count fixed to isolate residual variants. It cannot establish that sampled CE caused improvement over the historical BCE baseline. Any later objective comparison must use identical architectures, uniform candidate pools, negative counts, batching, and exposure, and implement the cited gSASRec calibration equation with its exact resolved parameters recorded. Vary negative count separately. A full architecture-by-objective factorial is deferred because it would dilute the present budget; do not claim its interactions have been measured. Loss-only alternatives remain eligible deployment choices even though they do not independently meet the selected research idea's two-user-failure requirement.

Sparse implementation: store normalized item rows in CSR and avoid any item-by-item matrix. For each prefix, obtain only its at-most-20-row Gram matrix and recent-anchor columns, mask equal IDs, and construct the weighted sparse sum. Cache fixed context features per training-visible sequence position when storage and sequence construction permit; otherwise process bounded batches and cache repeated windows. Candidate scoring gathers candidate text rows and computes sparse dot products; detach only fixed text state, preserving gradient to alpha. A simple rolling sum is insufficient because arrival or departure of an event can change maximum agreement and therefore the weights of all retained events. Recompute these weights or maintain a correctly tested dynamic maximum structure. Profile preprocessing, sparse operations, transfers, and chunk sizes. At full-catalog inference compute blockwise X*q, add collaborative logits, apply native historical-item exclusion, and maintain top-k. Record CPU preprocessing time separately and charge GPU-active work under the host's budget accounting.

Controls and budget: subtract all earlier charged training, diagnostics, debugging, and failed-trial GPU-seconds from 43,200; a new report does not reset the budget. Reserve one-sixth of the remainder for calibration, diagnostics, and parity checks, and divide the rest equally among four primary conditions and four categories. If remaining budget is R, each category-condition receives at most 5R/96 GPU-seconds. If the reserve cannot cover planned diagnostics, reduce the predeclared diagnostic sample before execution and disclose the reduction. Stop at the category cap or 200 epochs while preserving the existing validation/checkpoint schedule; time stopping may require discarding a partial epoch. Record completed epochs, updates, processed positions, total GPU cost, and every trial result. Conditions without valid results for all four categories are incomplete and cannot be ranked by partial macro scores. Equal time measures budget efficiency; unequal completed exposure limits mechanistic attribution. Do not silently add an equal-update retraining study. Reuse an incumbent only after verifying complete protocol and artifact compatibility; a historical scalar score is insufficient.

Frozen-model diagnostic reserve: on the selected anchored checkpoint, replace C's weights with recency-only r, anchor-only r*a, anchor-squared r*a², and recent-only weights r*1[age<3], using the same normalization and confidence convention. Also replace recent anchors with the earliest min(3,window_length) events and with an equally sized random subset of event positions drawn once per prefix from a deterministic analysis RNG seeded 42. Preserve the equal-ID exclusion. These are inference interventions on one trained model, not equally trained competitors; they can diagnose sensitivity but cannot establish which pooling rule would win after training. Training such alternatives requires a separately declared, charged follow-up family. A timestamp-value shuffle cannot affect this first algorithm because it uses event age rather than elapsed time; do not present that null intervention as evidence of temporal robustness. Shuffling event order changes sequential inputs and has different confounds, so it is excluded from the initial checks.

Duplicates and lexical shortcuts: measure repeated-ID frequency and training-only normalized-title duplicates. Normalize titles using the same lowercase tokenization and compare complete normalized titles, excluding empty strings; these are exact lexical groups, not verified product families. Aggregate support mass by event, distinct ID, and title group, and report concentration alongside residual magnitude. On the same frozen checkpoint, suppress equal-title cross-item matches and recompute the entire context, then compare support, scores, margins, and rank changes on identical diagnostic fixtures. Also inspect title-only, description-only, and removal of the most frequent retained tokens as predeclared frozen-feature perturbations where reserve permits; rebuild normalization consistently and report all outcomes. These interventions alter feature quality and scale and are not retraining controls. Approximate description clustering and one-vote-per-cluster training remain future experiments requiring a specified clustering algorithm and threshold. Amazon's older dataset documentation establishes a plausible near-duplicate mechanism, not its prevalence in this pinned benchmark. Do not modify input splits or introduce an internal chronological holdout; use training-only diagnostic fixtures and the existing authorized validation protocol.

Selection and uncertainty: use only pinned validation with 200 users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42, and equal-weight macro HR@10. Preserve candidate sets and the evaluator. Retain the incumbent on exact ties. Report all four category values, macro HR@10, training exposure, and GPU cost. One additional hit changes a category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. If authorized per-user hit indicators already exist, compute 10,000 paired category-stratified bootstrap replicates with separate analysis seed 42: resample users within each category, reuse each resample for both models, and average category differences equally. Report the percentile 95% interval. Otherwise state that the interval is unavailable; do not modify the evaluator to obtain it. Intervals condition on trained models and fixed candidates, omit training-seed and candidate variability, and do not correct validation winner selection. Report trial count and label conclusions exploratory and single-seed. Sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog quality.

Simulator: retain full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five/category, under the native protocol. Exclude historical IDs. Track direct-interest selections, useful-complement judgments, broad associations, duplication, unsupported use cases, and insufficient descriptive information separately wherever the simulator supplies such judgments. Never manufacture compatibility, dimensions, quantity, ownership, unmet needs, or diversity/conformity traits. Simulator feedback remains diagnostic and does not replace macro HR@10 selection. Lexical anchoring may favor substitutes or editions and suppress useful complements; explicitly examine this failure rather than assuming specificity always improves usefulness.

Adapter and predictor: retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, with batches (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors B x L. view.model must be the actual trained nn.Module and view.item_emb its collaborative embedding. Make log2feats return a packed tensor containing collaborative features and the at-most-20 causal context IDs at every position; pack IDs in float64 with exact integer-range checks and cast collaborative features back to their original dtype when scoring. Recover event ages from the ordered nonpadding window. Document whether predict_score receives position-aligned IDs, shared candidate lists, or per-position candidate matrices, and implement each required case without ambiguous broadcasting. Recompute the exact chosen lexical rule in predict_score. Preserve user_train, meta_data, and review_data without fabricating unavailable fields. Run finite-value and causal-prefix checks on augmented features and margins on fused logits; embedding cosine remains descriptive, and item-category breakdowns remain explicitly unavailable. Add defined support activation, anchor attenuation, effective pooling size, duplicate concentration, residual scale, and rank-change metrics. Restore model training/evaluation state after probes.

Update the predictor writer to emit the matching architecture and load category-specific weights, CSR text artifacts, row mappings, configuration, calibration A, learned amplitude, pooling rule, padding, truncation, and routing. Keep generated working/predict.py's required API and supplied candidate order. Do not apply an extra seen-item filter to pinned candidate scoring; native full-catalog simulator exclusion is a separate operation. Verify score and candidate-order parity against the training scorer on deterministic training-visible fixtures covering empty histories, missing text, repeated IDs, one distinct item, all-equal titles, disconnected old clusters, three repeated anchor IDs, short windows, and mixed-category routes. Test that masked future events do not alter earlier context. Record a numerical tolerance appropriate to the resolved scoring dtype and any failures. All execution remains host work and consumes the applicable shared budget.

Assessment details, scores in originality/future potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty order: recent anchoring 3/6/7/5/5. Originality positive: the concentration-controlled anchor comparison is explicit; negative: recent-interest matching and gated lexical fusion are established. Potential positive: it provides an inspectable baseline for later routing; negative: lexical brittleness and sparse activation limit generality. User alignment positive: directly targets broad associations and stale evidence; negative: it cannot identify current needs and may favor duplicates. Model alignment positive: shared multi-negative training and residual diagnostics target observed separation weaknesses; negative: anchoring has no established causal connection to those training errors. Difficulty positive: fixed sparse features retain SASRec; negative: causal reweighting, caching, diagnostics, and predictor parity require substantial work. Generalized-BCE control 2/7/3/8/3. Originality positive: a clear matched application; negative: the method is established. Potential positive: inexpensive and reusable; negative: task gains remain unknown. User alignment positive: better discrimination could improve the list; negative: it supplies no explicit mechanism for two diagnosed user failures. Model alignment positive: directly investigates sampled-loss calibration; negative: overconfidence is not established by the supplied margins. Difficulty positive: scoring architecture stays unchanged; negative: calibration and loss-versus-negative-count controls must be correct. Learned routing 4/7/8/6/7. Originality positive: permits a task-specific disagreement gate; negative: long/short-term routing has substantial prior art. Potential positive: can represent returning and changing interests; negative: latent intent remains weakly identified. User alignment positive: explicitly models specific recent versus persistent interests; negative: intent is not compatibility or unmet need. Model alignment positive: flexible representations could improve pair ordering; negative: additional capacity can memorize training pairs. Difficulty positive: uses permitted inputs with no pretrained model; negative: architectural serialization, added parameters, and a larger control family increase cost.
idea.pseudocode:
CONFIG: categories = FOUR_BASELINE_CATEGORIES
CONFIG: preprocessing_seed = 0; training_seed = 42
CONFIG: window = 20; anchors = 3; decay = 5; negatives = 32
CONFIG: epochs = existing_environment_default_200
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']

# Fixed text rows are fitted only on items appearing in training histories.
# CSR rows are L2-normalized; padding, missing text, and out-of-scope rows are zero.
def lexical_context(prefix, vectors, mode):
    events = last_nonpadding_events(prefix, 20)
    if len(events) == 0:
        return sparse_zero_vector(), 0.0
    V = vectors[events]
    G = sparse_pairwise_cosines(V)  # at most 20 x 20
    eligible = events[:, None] != events[None, :]
    G = where(eligible, clamp(G, 0.0, 1.0), 0.0)
    u = row_max(G, default=0.0)
    anchor_columns = last_event_positions(events, min(3, len(events)))
    a = row_max(G[:, anchor_columns], default=0.0)
    ages = len(events) - 1 - arange(len(events))
    r = exp(-ages / 5.0)
    if mode == 'starting':
        w = r * u
    elif mode == 'anchored':
        w = r * u * a
    elif mode == 'squared':
        w = r * u * u
    else:
        raise ValueError(mode)
    q = l2_normalize_or_zero(sparse_weighted_sum(V, w), eps=1e-8)
    c = sum(w) / max(sum(r), 1e-8)
    return q, c

# Call separately for each supervised causal prefix, never including its target.
def score(h, q, c, candidate_ids, condition):
    base = dot(h, item_emb(candidate_ids))
    if condition == 'objective_only':
        return base
    alpha = 2.0 * saved_A * sigmoid(amplitude_parameter)
    return base + alpha * c * sparse_dot(q, tfidf[candidate_ids])

remaining = 43200 - all_previous_charged_GPU_seconds
reserve = remaining / 6
category_condition_cap = (remaining - reserve) / (4 * 4)

for condition in ['objective_only', 'starting', 'anchored', 'squared']:
    for category in FOUR_BASELINE_CATEGORIES:
        initialize_identical_baseline_backbone(seed=42)
        negative_rng = dedicated_generator(seed=42)
        if condition != 'objective_only':
            initialize_amplitude(log(0.05 / 0.95))
        for batch in unchanged_category_loader(category):
            h = causal_sasrec_features(batch.sequence)
            if condition == 'objective_only':
                q, c = None, None
            else:
                q, c = contexts_for_every_causal_position(
                    batch.sequence, mode=condition)
            candidates, mask, eligible_positions = positive_plus_uniform_negatives(
                count=32, without_replacement=True,
                exclude='padding,target,observed_prefix_only', rng=negative_rng)
            logits = score(h, q, c, candidates, condition)
            loss = masked_CE(logits, positive_index=0, temperature=1,
                             average_over=eligible_positions)
            optimize(loss)
            honor_existing_checkpoint_schedule_and_category_time_cap()
        save_trial_local_weights_config_text_and_matching_predictor()
        verify_generated_predictor_parity_on_training_visible_fixtures()
        run_actual_model_DiagnosisProbe_with_fused_scores()
    record_complete_four_category_host_validation_or_mark_incomplete()

# Frozen-checkpoint interventions are diagnostics, not retrained competitors:
# recent-only, recency-only, anchor-only, anchor-squared, oldest/random anchors,
# and exclusion of equal-normalized-title matches, within the declared reserve.
# Recompute support and normalization consistently for each intervention.
# Select by unchanged pinned macro validation HR@10; retain incumbent on ties.
# Bootstrap only already-authorized per-user validation outcomes, if available.
# Never access hidden test labels or modify the host evaluator.

originality.positive: The explicit comparison of recent anchoring with squared-support concentration makes the proposed mechanism testable.
originality.negative: Recent-interest matching, lexical pooling, and gated additive scoring are established; the contribution is incremental.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inspectable baseline separating historical resemblance, recent relevance, and evidence attenuation before introducing learned routing.
future_potential.negative: Lexical brittleness, duplicate wording, sparse activation, and suppression of useful complements may limit generality.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains SASRec and fixed sparse text features without a learned encoder or pretrained weights.
code_difficulty.negative: History-dependent maxima prevent simple rolling-sum updates; efficient causal computation, controlled diagnostics, exact feature packing, and generated-predictor parity require substantial care.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention recommendation backbone retained in the proposal.
limitations: Does not establish current usefulness, compatibility, or unmet needs from purchase histories.

related_work.title: ICSRec
contributions: The supplied summary describes contrastive learning of latent intentions from sliding subsequences.
limitations: Same-target alignment is an assumption about shared intention.
Does not validate fixed lexical recent-anchor gating under the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Hierarchical long/short-term modeling
contributions: The supplied summary describes multiple historical preference vectors matched to recent interests using temporal information.
limitations: Learned routing adds complexity.
Its reported mechanism does not establish that the proposed lexical weights improve this benchmark.

related_work.title: Parallel Attention Network
contributions: Models long- and short-term interests and motivates considering more than the last interaction.
limitations: Does not establish three events as the correct anchor count or validate multiplicative TF–IDF agreement.

related_work.title: Search-based User Interest Modeling with Lifelong Sequential Behavior Data for Click-Through Rate Prediction
contributions: Retrieves historical behaviors relevant to a candidate item, motivating selective historical aggregation.
limitations: Uses a candidate-conditioned query rather than the proposal's recent-history anchors.
Its task and evaluation do not establish gains under the pinned RecHarness protocol.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Studies overconfidence associated with negative-sampled BCE and proposes generalized BCE.
Provides an established objective alternative to retain for matched follow-up comparisons.
limitations: Reported improvements combine loss calibration with more negatives, requiring controls to separate their effects.
The supplied training margins do not themselves establish overconfidence.
An objective change alone does not explicitly resolve both broad-association and stale-interest failures.

related_work.title: Sampled-softmax analysis
contributions: Connects sampled-softmax optimization with negative weighting and ranking behavior.
limitations: Does not establish improved macro HR@10 on these four datasets.
Sampled probabilities are not full-softmax probabilities, and implicit-feedback negatives can include latent positives.

related_work.title: Amazon product data documentation
contributions: Documents near-identical products and merged-review behavior in historical Amazon data, motivating duplicate-sensitive diagnostics.
limitations: Does not establish the presence or prevalence of duplicates in this pinned benchmark.
Provides no authorization to retrieve additional datasets or unavailable review fields.

related_work.title: Scikit-learn text feature extraction documentation
contributions: Documents TF–IDF representations and text feature extraction relevant to reproducible lexical preprocessing.
limitations: TF–IDF does not guarantee semantic specificity or remove all brand and product-family boilerplate.

related_work.title: SciPy CSR matrix documentation
contributions: Documents sparse row operations and matrix-vector products useful for bounded-memory context construction and catalog scoring.
limitations: Does not supply an incremental algorithm for history-dependent maximum-agreement weights.
Actual preprocessing, transfers, and scoring costs require profiling.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains why sampled-candidate evaluation can rank recommenders differently from full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator.
Supports limiting conclusions to HR@10 against the specified fixed negative candidates.
